t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup on a deep navy background with a faint square blueprint grid. Eyebrow with a short terminated rule, then a large light-weight pale-blue sans headline. Below, a three-column table with hairline row rules and numbered rows, all cells in monospace, for <CONTENT>. Between the columns, vertical double-line pipe manifolds in pale blue-white branch into every row with rounded elbows, ending in P&ID valve symbols and arrows that point into the next cell. Flat line art, no glow.
signature_idea: The table is plumbed: pipe manifolds between the columns carry each auditor's row through a valve to the place it is answered.
strengths: pipe manifolds give a plain table a real visual idea tied to the product
strict navy monochrome blueprint is calm and precise
mono standards codes suit the brand
rows read clearly left to right
weaknesses: no steel-blue pipe as prompted; pipes are pale white so there is no accent
valve branches are decorative; rows do not actually map one-to-one to answers
mono for all body cells is dense and harder to read
invented regulatory clauses and dates read as fact
dark-only treatment loses the limestone half of the palette
brand_fit_why: Navy blueprint, light headline, mono codes and square corners fit, but the missing steel-blue accent, all-mono density and decorative valves cost a point.
